author: CC (second instance) — design session with Akien; his ruling, ratified in session

text:
THE CORRECTION THAT OPENED IT — AKIEN, 2026-08-05, reading the brief: 'similarity edges are never stored... i didn't ask for that. why's that there? i thought that's what the trees were for?' He was right, and the paper trail confirms it.

PROVENANCE, TRACED. Two claims had been welded into one sentence. (a) IS AKIEN'S AND IS EARNED: the conventional build reached 70,000 words / 2.5M bigram edges / over 30 seconds per edge update, cost growing with the corpus — 'the wall is storing edges at all' (memory-shape.json, the_measured_history_that_motivates_all_of_it). (b) IS CC'S LEAP, never a ruling: 'therefore store no similarity structure at all; recompute cosine every walk.' Settled in memory-shape.json key edges__answers_open_question_3 ('SETTLED BY THE SHEAR, not by preference'), and older still in tickets/librarian-graph-trees.json. It is now physics in the running code (cairn/librarian/trees.py:17) pinned by a proof named test_no_edge_table_exists. ONLY (a) IS SUPPORTED BY THE 30-SECOND NUMBER.

THE COST CHECK THAT SETTLED (b) BEAT A STRAWMAN. It compared ~10,000 entry rewrites for articulated edges at degree 4 against '2,500 x 5,000 = 12.5M if similarity edges were materialized AT FULL DENSITY.' Full density is a complete graph — every leaf linked to every other leaf. Nobody proposed that. A bounded kNN graph at k=8 over a 5,000-leaf tree is ~40k edges total; a calve moving 2,500 leaves rewrites tens of thousands of entries — the SAME ORDER as the ~10,000 already accepted for articulated edges. (CC's arithmetic, not measured — a hypothesis under Law 3, and cheap to check.) The comparison that killed stored similarity structure beat the worst possible version of it, not the one that would actually be built.

THE BUILD TOOK THE BAD HALF OF EACH. nearest() at trees.py:207 loads every row in the tree and sorts by cosine — a full linear scan, no traversal anywhere. Across trees, routing is greedy by attractor: one choice, no backtrack, no exhaustiveness. So it pays SCAN prices for TRAVERSAL-grade recall. Brief §2.8's 'manufactured novelty' is not a subtle risk in that arrangement — it is the direct consequence of the only traversal-shaped step in the system being the one place with no fallback. And §2.4's 'the vector IS the path' is unearned: the 'sequence of choices' is exactly two comparisons, which tree and which leaf. That is a ROUTED SCAN, not a walk.

THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: DERIVED-ONLY MEANS THE INDEX CANNOT LEARN. The corpus grows, but the retrieval MECHANISM is stateless — identical cost and identical quality at query #1 and at query #1,000,000. The brief's h_t argument is only ever about deposits (more nodes in the tree), which is the shallow half. AKIEN'S FRAMING: 'where we get the speed and the compiled inference is by having the weights in the trees. that's what the indexing is.' Weights are the other half — paths that resolve get stronger, so the ROUTE improves with use and not merely the contents. Inference spent once COMPILES INTO THE INDEX ITSELF rather than into a row a brute-force scan must still find. A cosine scan is not an index; it is the absence of one. The current design has no index at all — it has a partition.

THE RECURSION THAT FALLS OUT. Apply the strata ladder (model / tree / code) to retrieval itself and the three tiers are: WEIGHTED PATH (compiled, near-free, for routes that have proven out) / SCAN (thorough, slower, for when the weighted path comes up short) / INFERENCE (genuine novelty). Retrieval stops being one mechanism and becomes a learning block in its own right, measured by the same migration rate. That is §3.5's recursion actually landing somewhere instead of being an observation about the org chart.

THE SCAN'S VIRTUE IS RECALL — CC HAD UNDERSOLD IT. An exhaustive comparison cannot miss a leaf; a traversal reaches only what it is linked to. So it is not 'traversal good, scan bad' — it is a recall/cost tradeoff, and the thorough one belongs in the design as the thing you FALL BACK TO, never as the thing you replace.

ON 'LIKE SEARCHES' — AKIEN'S QUESTION, ANSWERED. He asked whether a LIKE search over the embedding blobs was the second mechanism. Mechanically no: LIKE is substring matching over characters; a vector blob is 768 float32s, and two vectors at cosine 0.99 have essentially unrelated byte patterns because small numeric differences rewrite mantissa bytes wholesale — so substring-matching the blob finds nothing useful. BUT the operation he wanted — scan everything, spend the time, miss nothing — is a flat/brute-force EXACT search, and it is ALREADY what trees.py does; it simply is not spelled LIKE. AND the instinct maps to a real technique: LOCALITY-SENSITIVE HASHING turns each vector into a short bit-string such that NEAR VECTORS SHARE A PREFIX, so a literal prefix LIKE does retrieve near neighbours in one index seek (SimHash, random-projection LSH). HELD as a known alternative for tier 1 if the weighted trees do not earn their keep — not a build.

THE SECOND MECHANISM IS ACTUALLY TWO TOOLS, and they fail differently. EXHAUSTIVE VECTOR SCAN: thorough, cannot miss, cost grows with the corpus. LEXICAL SEARCH OVER NODE CONTENT: the real LIKE — catches exact terms, names, identifiers and quoted phrases that embeddings routinely smear away. The lexical one is the only one of the three that finds what vectors STRUCTURALLY CANNOT.

THE RULING — THREE LAYERS, NOT TWO. From Akien's UU description: 'the embedding record is a blob and points back to it's memory. they point at each other', and 'the nodes can contain links into a list of VECTORS belonging to each node.' So: NODE — the claim, provenance, standing; has an identity; belongs to no tree. EMBEDDING — a vector, its own record, pointing to its node and the node back at it; MANY PER NODE. LEAF — an address in a tree, pointing at an EMBEDDING, carrying the weights and the two-way articulated links. The brief's leaf currently does two unrelated jobs at once: it holds the vector AND it holds the connections. Splitting the vector out into its own layer is the move.

WHAT THE THIRD LAYER RESOLVES. (1) §4.4 open item 1, 'where does the vector live' — neither node nor leaf; it is its own layer that both point at. (2) §4.2's defence of leaf-side vectors ('otherwise every tree would place that node at identical coordinates') stops being load-bearing: a node with several embeddings gets several placements natively. (3) §2.5's MEASURED diagram defect becomes a solved case — a flow diagram scored 0.4943 against a prose question it directly answers, and the brief's fix was 'a prose rendering before embedding.' With ONE vector per node you must CHOOSE which rendering wins; with MANY you keep both, raw and prose-rendered, and the scan sees both. (4) The thorough tier gets a table to run on: the exhaustive scan runs over the embedding layer DIRECTLY, needing no trees at all — which is exactly the independent second mechanism Akien described.

AND IT STRENGTHENS THE SHEAR PROPERTY. A calve still never touches a node. It MAY touch embedding back-references — and that is fine, because an embedding is a DERIVED artifact: damage it and you regenerate it. A node cannot be regenerated. So the only layer index maintenance can reach is precisely the layer that is cheap to rebuild. That is a better version of the argument §4.4 already makes, not a weakening of it.

THE COSTS, NAMED. (1) Weights that strengthen on resolution are a POSITIVE FEEDBACK LOOP, and §2.7 is already a story about one. A wrong route that resolves once gets stronger and is likelier to be chosen next time — manufactured novelty with a ratchet on it. So weights need the asymmetry already required of gates in §3.2: COUNTER-EVIDENCE LOWERS A WEIGHT FASTER THAN CONFIRMATION RAISES IT. Same principle, one layer down. (2) Weights are stored state that must survive a renumbering, so by the ticket's own boundary rule ('an edge that must survive a shear is an edge you are storing') they land ARTICULATED-SIDE and the existing two-way shear machinery already covers them — no new mechanism. (3) The thorough tier is affordable only because it fires RARELY; scan every embedding in the corpus and you are back at §2.4's 7.7 GB, the number that 'fits nowhere.' HOW OFTEN THE FALLBACK FIRES IS ITSELF A DIAL — if it fires constantly, the weighted index is not learning and the thing that died has been rebuilt.

PGVECTOR IS PRECEDENT, NOT INTENTION. AKIEN: 'pgvector is what we did in UU.' The brief files it as 'a filed edge waiting on a real load. It is not installed.' It is the off-the-shelf answer for the thorough tier and it does both exact and approximate search. Its status should move from speculative-future to precedent-with-a-job.

BUILD ORDER, RATIFIED IN SESSION ('i agree with everything here'). (1) THE EMBEDDING LAYER — cheapest, unblocks everything else, and it is a REFINEMENT of step 1 in memory-shape.json's build_order_for_the_embeddings_generator rather than a detour around it. (2) WEIGHTS IN THE TREES — the compiled inference, the actual index; second because it needs the asymmetry guard, and the ticket already scopes it there ('edge weights (paths that resolve get stronger) are a real mechanism and the natural correction for a bad router, but they are the second build'). (3) LEXICAL SEARCH OVER CONTENT — nearly free, and the only one that finds what vectors cannot. LSH held as a tier-1 alternative, not a build.

FALSIFIER 7 GETS TEETH. As currently designed, composing over a walked path means averaging vectors already selected for being near the query, so the composed vector lands near the query close to tautologically — CC expects that falsifier to FAIL as specified. With weights there is something LEARNED to compose with, so the test measures an actual claim.

WHAT THIS OBSOLETES. memory-shape.json key edges__answers_open_question_3 is SUPERSEDED IN ITS SECOND HALF: both kinds of edge still exist and the shear is still the boundary, but 'similarity edges are derived at walk time, never materialized' is no longer the settled answer — a weighted, bounded, STORED similarity structure IS the index. Law 9: no past artifact outranks him now. The brief's §2.4, §2.6 and the Appendix entry ('similarity edge: derived at walk time from leaf vectors; never stored') all carry the superseded claim, as does NoveltyDrivenGraphTreeExpansion.md §6.2, and trees.py plus test_no_edge_table_exists are the physics holding it in place.

APPROVED, AKIEN, 2026-08-05 — THE PROOF IS RETIRED DELIBERATELY. His word: 'approved'. test_no_edge_table_exists is a GREEN proof actively pinning the superseded half of the decision, so it must not be allowed to simply start failing during the build: retiring it is a NAMED ACT, not a casualty. Under Law 4, a rule that matters is enforced by physics — which means the physics currently enforces the OLD ruling, and replacing a rule means replacing its ENFORCEMENT in the same breath, never leaving the corpus with a tooth that bites the new design. AND THE REPLACEMENT MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE RETIREMENT: the original proof exists to fence off the 2.5M bigram wall, and deleting it without a successor would quietly give back the protection it was built to provide. The successor tooth should assert the NEW invariant — that a stored similarity structure is BOUNDED and WEIGHTED, and that nothing full-density can be registered — so the fence stays up and merely learns to admit the index.

PENDING — THE BRIEF. Earlier this session the brief was synced to the 2026-08-05 PDF: subtitle to 'A technical brief', Status to final, the 'since we adopted our new approach' line in How to read this, and the §2.1 rewrite to 'differently in the name of different needs'. THE FINAL UPDATE — this ruling — IS NOT YET APPLIED and is the next act, to be compacted first.
